channel.title: Circuit Weekly
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news: the outlet, the events and the quotes are invented; the places are real so the map can show them.

item.title: Chipmaker unveils a laptop processor with all-day battery life
item.description: A chipmaker has unveiled a new laptop processor it says can run for 20 hours on a single charge. The first laptops using it will go on sale in the spring.

item.title: Robot vacuum learns to climb stairs
item.description: A home robotics company has shown a robot vacuum that can climb stairs using two small legs. It will cost about 1,500 dollars when it launches next year.

item.title: Startup launches satellite internet service for farms
item.description: A startup has launched a satellite internet service designed for farms in remote areas. It says the service reaches speeds of 100 megabits per second.

item.title: Smartphone battery breakthrough promises a week of use
item.description: Researchers at a battery firm say a new silicon design could let phones last a week between charges. The company hopes to start production in 2027.

item.title: Seoul tests self-driving buses on night routes
item.description: Seoul has started testing self-driving buses on two night routes. The city says the buses will help night workers get home when other transport has stopped.

item.title: Translation earbuds now handle 40 languages
item.description: A new pair of earbuds can translate conversations in 40 languages in real time, its maker says. “Travel should not stop at the language barrier,” the company said.

item.title: Open AI model runs on an ordinary laptop
item.description: Researchers have released an AI model small enough to run on an ordinary laptop. They say it needs about 8 gigabytes of memory and works without an internet connection.

item.title: Handheld games console sells 2 million units in its first week
item.description: A new handheld games console sold 2 million units in its first week, its maker says. Shops in Tokyo reported long queues on launch day.

item.title: Barcelona trials a fleet of delivery robots
item.description: Twenty delivery robots have started carrying parcels through two districts of Barcelona. The trial will run for six months.

item.title: Swedish recycling plant recovers gold from old phones
item.description: A recycling plant in Sweden says it can recover 1 kilogram of gold from 40,000 old phones. The company wants to process 2 million phones a year.

item.title: Data centre near Reykjavik runs on wind and geothermal power
item.description: A data centre powered by wind and geothermal energy has opened near Reykjavik. Its owners say it uses 30 percent less energy for cooling than a typical site.

item.title: Medicine-carrying drones expand across Rwanda
item.description: Drones now deliver medicine to 400 health centres across Rwanda, the operator says. The average flight takes about 30 minutes.

item.title: Smart glasses show live subtitles for deaf users
item.description: A company in Berlin has shown smart glasses that display live subtitles of conversations. “We want everyone to follow the conversation,” a spokesperson said.

item.title: Tech giants agree on a common charger standard for laptops
item.description: Several large technology companies have agreed on a common charging standard for laptops. Chargers will work across brands from next year.
